summary: The session component is the loop's state and persistence substrate. ToolCache and LlmCache avoid redundant act and reason work; EditHistory records file edits as branchable EditCheckpoints for undo/redo/timeline; the CheckpointManager snapshots the whole TaskCheckpoint (step, iteration, messages, tool logs, budget) via delta writes for resume; EncryptionManager protects data at rest with AES-256-GCM; LocalFirstCoordinator caches responses offline; ChatStore persists encrypted conversations.
context_basis: recommendations were formed with src/session/ read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in cache.rs ToolCache/LlmCache/CacheManager, edit_history.rs EditCheckpoint/EditHistory, checkpoint.rs TaskCheckpoint/CheckpointDelta/CheckpointManager, encryption.rs EncryptionManager, local_first.rs, and chat_store.rs.

examples.title: Cache a read-only tool result
examples.intent: Skip re-executing a tool whose inputs have not changed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolCache keys on tool_name+args_json and returns a hit within TTL, so the act stage returns instantly and the loop spends its budget elsewhere.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a read node reveals its cache card; a hit lights the shortcut edge to the stored value.
touch_interaction.visual: A cache hit shows a lightning badge; the node skips its execution spinner.

examples.mini_scenario: A repeated grep_search returns from ToolCache in microseconds instead of scanning the tree again.
examples.pitfall: Caching without mtime-based staleness checks serves outdated file contents to the loop.

examples.title: Invalidate cache entries by path
examples.intent: Drop only the cache entries a mutation could have affected.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: invalidate_path removes every ToolCache entry containing the touched path, so post-write reads re-run against fresh state without nuking unrelated cached results.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks a write node's edge across the cache to clear entries for that path only.
touch_interaction.visual: Only path-matching cache cards fade out; unrelated cards stay intact.

examples.mini_scenario: After editing config.rs, only config.rs cache entries are dropped so its next read is fresh.
examples.pitfall: Over-broad invalidation clears the whole cache and forfeits the savings on unrelated reads.

examples.title: Evict expired and LRU entries on overflow
examples.intent: Keep the cache from growing without bound.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: evict_expired purges expired entries and, at max_entries, removes an LRU slice, so the cache stays inside its budget without stalling the loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the cache node compacts it, visibly dropping the oldest and expired cards.
touch_interaction.visual: Expired cards grey and fall away; the entry-count gauge settles back under the max.

examples.mini_scenario: The cache reaches max_entries; eviction removes 10% oldest so new results still fit.
examples.pitfall: Setting max_entries too low thrashes the cache and negates its benefit under a busy loop.

examples.title: Match a semantic LLM cache hit
examples.intent: Reuse a prior LLM response for a near-identical prompt.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: LlmCache::lookup matches on cosine similarity of embeddings plus a context_hash and model match, so a repeated reason turn can be served from cache and skip a billable call.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the Reason node shows nearby cached prompts by similarity distance.
touch_interaction.visual: Candidate cache cards orbit by closeness; a match snaps in with a similarity score badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A re-asked question with the same context hash and model returns the cached answer, saving a turn.
examples.pitfall: Ignoring context_hash serves an answer computed under a different context and misleads the loop.

examples.title: Snapshot a file before it changes
examples.intent: Capture the exact prior state so any edit can be undone.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EditHistory::create_checkpoint records a FileSnapshot (path, content, size, hash) tagged with an EditAction, giving the loop a durable rollback point per mutation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a write node drops a snapshot pin capturing the file's pre-edit state.
touch_interaction.visual: A camera-pin badge appears on the timeline with the file hash.

examples.mini_scenario: Before applying a patch, the loop snapshots the file so /undo can restore it exactly.
examples.pitfall: Snapshotting after the edit instead of before loses the original content and breaks undo.

examples.title: Undo the last edit checkpoint
examples.intent: Roll the workspace back to the state before a bad edit.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EditHistory::undo steps the current pointer back and restores the FileSnapshot, letting the loop recover from a wrong turn without redoing the whole task.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks the timeline left to step the pointer back and restore the prior snapshot.
touch_interaction.visual: The current-checkpoint marker slides back and the restored file card flashes.

examples.mini_scenario: An edit breaks the build; /undo restores the pre-edit snapshot and the loop retries a different fix.
examples.pitfall: Undoing past a git commit checkpoint without accounting for it desyncs the working tree from history.

examples.title: Branch the edit timeline on a new edit
examples.intent: Preserve alternate edit paths after an undo.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: create_checkpoint truncates future history on the current branch when a new edit follows an undo, so the timeline models a tree of what-if edit paths the loop explored.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws a branch edge from an earlier checkpoint to spawn an alternate edit path.
touch_interaction.visual: The timeline forks into a labeled branch line with its own checkpoint pins.

examples.mini_scenario: After undoing, a different edit forks a new branch so the abandoned path is not lost.
examples.pitfall: Assuming a linear timeline after undo silently discards the branch the loop meant to keep.

examples.title: Render the edit timeline
examples.intent: Show the loop's edit history so a user can pick a restore point.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EditHistory::timeline emits TimelineEntry rows (id, is_current, action, timestamp, branch), giving /timeline the data to render the loop's mutation history.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the timeline node expands the full list of edit checkpoints with actions and branches.
touch_interaction.visual: Each entry is a labeled pin; the current one is highlighted and branches are colored distinctly.

examples.mini_scenario: The user opens /timeline, sees every edit checkpoint, and jumps to one with goto.
examples.pitfall: Rendering timestamps without branch labels makes divergent edit paths indistinguishable.

examples.title: Save the loop's TaskCheckpoint
examples.intent: Persist enough state to resume the loop after interruption.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CheckpointManager::save writes a TaskCheckpoint holding current_step, current_iteration, messages, tool_calls, errors, and cumulative budget, so continue_execution can rehydrate the loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the control hub drops a task-checkpoint pin capturing the whole loop state.
touch_interaction.visual: A save pin shows step/iteration and a token-total badge, pulsing once on write.

examples.mini_scenario: Mid-task the manager saves a checkpoint; after a crash, load restores the loop's step and messages.
examples.pitfall: Persisting messages but not cumulative budget lets a resumed loop exceed its original ceiling.

examples.title: Write incremental checkpoint deltas
examples.intent: Persist progress cheaply on every turn without rewriting the whole checkpoint.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: save prefers CheckpointDelta writes (new messages, tool calls, errors since a base version) and compacts every 24 deltas or over 512KB, keeping per-turn persistence lightweight.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the checkpoint node shows a stack of delta layers over the base snapshot.
touch_interaction.visual: Delta layers stack thin; at the compaction threshold they fold into a fresh base card.

examples.mini_scenario: Each turn appends a small delta; after 24 the manager compacts them into a new base for fast loads.
examples.pitfall: Never compacting deltas makes load slow and fragile as the delta chain grows unbounded.

examples.title: Load a checkpoint and apply deltas
examples.intent: Rebuild the exact loop state a resumed task needs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CheckpointManager::load reads the base and replays all CheckpointDeltas to reconstruct the TaskCheckpoint, so continue_execution restarts the loop at the right step and iteration.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks a saved checkpoint pin onto the canvas to rehydrate the loop from it.
touch_interaction.visual: The base card and its delta layers merge into a single restored state, then the loop resumes.

examples.mini_scenario: On resume, load replays the deltas to reconstruct the messages and progress, and the loop continues.
examples.pitfall: Applying deltas out of version order reconstructs a corrupt or stale loop state.

examples.title: Recover a corrupted checkpoint
examples.intent: Keep the loop resumable even if a checkpoint file is damaged.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: recover_from_corruption tries the .json.bak backup and otherwise creates a fresh checkpoint, so a torn write does not permanently strand the task.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a corrupted checkpoint pin offers restore-from-backup or start-fresh options.
touch_interaction.visual: A damaged pin shows a red crack; recovery heals it green or spawns a new blank pin.

examples.mini_scenario: A checkpoint is truncated by a crash; recovery loads the .json.bak and the loop resumes.
examples.pitfall: Silently starting fresh without surfacing the loss can drop hours of loop progress unnoticed.

examples.title: Encrypt session data at rest
examples.intent: Protect persisted conversations and checkpoints from disk snooping.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EncryptionManager::encrypt wraps bytes with AES-256-GCM and a random nonce; the ChatStore and checkpoints write ciphertext, so the loop's persistent substrate is confidential.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the persistence node toggles its encryption shield on the stored data cards.
touch_interaction.visual: Encrypted cards render with a lock glyph; unencrypted ones show an open lock warning.

examples.mini_scenario: A saved chat is AES-256-GCM encrypted before hitting disk and decrypted only in-process on load.
examples.pitfall: Reusing a nonce across encryptions under the same key breaks GCM's security guarantee.

examples.title: Derive the key from the OS keychain
examples.intent: Bootstrap encryption without a hard-coded key.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EncryptionManager::load_from_keychain reads the passphrase from the OS keychain and derive_key runs PBKDF2 with a per-install salt, so the loop's crypto substrate self-initializes securely.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the persistence node shows the key source (keychain) feeding the encryption shield.
touch_interaction.visual: A key-ring badge lights when the keychain provides the passphrase; a fallback shows an ephemeral badge.

examples.mini_scenario: On startup the manager pulls the passphrase from the keychain and derives the session key via PBKDF2.
examples.pitfall: Falling back to an ephemeral key without warning means data written this session cannot be decrypted later.

examples.title: Persist the conversation to the ChatStore
examples.intent: Save the loop's message history so a named session can be resumed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ChatStore::save writes a SavedChat (name, saved_at, model, messages) atomically and encrypted, so resume_named_session can restore the loop's conversation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the history strip saves it as a named, encrypted session card.
touch_interaction.visual: A named session card slots into the store shelf with a lock glyph and timestamp.

examples.mini_scenario: The user saves the current chat by name; later resume_named_session decrypts and reloads the messages.
examples.pitfall: A non-atomic write interrupted mid-save can leave a truncated, undecryptable chat file.

examples.title: List sessions, skipping tampered files
examples.intent: Show resumable sessions without crashing on a bad file.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ChatStore::list returns ChatSummary rows and skips corrupted or tamper-failed files, so the loop can present valid resume points and ignore the rest.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the store shelf fans out the saved session cards; corrupt ones are omitted.
touch_interaction.visual: Valid session cards render clean; tampered files simply do not appear.

examples.mini_scenario: One chat file fails its auth tag; list silently skips it and shows the remaining valid sessions.
examples.pitfall: Listing a file that fails decryption as if valid then errors on load, confusing the resume flow.

examples.title: Cache responses for local-first offline use
examples.intent: Serve prior responses and track bandwidth saved when offline.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: LocalFirstCoordinator::cache_response stores responses with size tracking and stats reports bandwidth_saved_bytes, so the loop can prefer cached data and quantify savings.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the persistence node surfaces a bandwidth-saved gauge from the local-first cache.
touch_interaction.visual: A savings gauge grows as cached responses are reused instead of refetched.

examples.mini_scenario: A repeated response is served from the local cache and /stats reports the bytes saved.
examples.pitfall: Unbounded FIFO growth of the local cache eventually evicts the very entries the loop reuses most.

examples.title: Report cache hit rate in stats
examples.intent: Make the cache's contribution to loop efficiency measurable.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CacheStats (entry_count, total_size_bytes, hit_rate) surfaces in /stats, letting the loop and operator see whether caching is actually saving turns and budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the cache node opens its stats card with hit rate and size.
touch_interaction.visual: A dial shows hit rate; green when high, amber when the cache is barely helping.

examples.mini_scenario: The /stats view shows a 60% tool-cache hit rate, confirming the cache is trimming redundant acts.
examples.pitfall: Reporting entry_count as a health metric without hit_rate hides a cache that stores much but hits little.

examples.title: Checkpoint on a git commit action
examples.intent: Anchor the edit timeline to the repository's own history.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: An EditCheckpoint with EditAction::GitCommit records the git_hash and dirty/staged/modified file state, aligning the loop's undo timeline with the real VCS boundary.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing after a commit drops a git-anchor pin that marks a hard timeline boundary.
touch_interaction.visual: The git pin renders with a commit-hash badge and a heavier boundary line.

examples.mini_scenario: After a commit, the timeline gets a git-anchored checkpoint so undo knows where the committed baseline is.
examples.pitfall: Treating a git-anchored checkpoint like an ordinary undo point can rewind past a commit and confuse the tree.

examples.title: Zeroize the key on drop
examples.intent: Ensure the encryption key never lingers in memory after use.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EncryptionManager's Drop impl zeroizes the key when the manager is dropped, so the loop's crypto substrate leaves no key residue for a memory scrape.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the persistence node away at session end wipes its key glyph in a visible scrub.
touch_interaction.visual: The key badge dissolves to zeros as the node is torn down.

examples.mini_scenario: At session end the manager drops and its key bytes are zeroized before the allocation is freed.
examples.pitfall: Copying the key into a struct without matching zeroization leaves a plaintext key copy behind.
